CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for evaluation of anxiety management, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, expressing ongoing concerns regarding his anxiety and sleep disturbances. He reports that while he has made a conscious effort to taper his use of lorazepam, now utilizing it only 2-3 times per week, he continues to experience significant difficulty initiating sleep. Despite the tapering, he notes that nighttime anxiety remains pronounced, leading to an average of only 4-5 hours of sleep per night. He has increased his melatonin dosage to 10 mg at bedtime, which he feels has had a marginal improvement in sleep onset but has not significantly extended his total sleep duration.
The patient acknowledges that his fatigue has worsened, particularly in the afternoons, which he attributes to both his disrupted sleep patterns and the stress associated with his current work projects. He reports an increase in the frequency of his headaches, now occurring three times weekly, with a notable escalation in intensity. He has continued to take amitriptyline at 20 mg nightly, along with ibuprofen as needed, but is seeking additional preventive strategies. Mr. Smith has initiated acupuncture sessions once a week, expressing hope that this will provide relief from his headache symptoms.
He has been diligent about maintaining his yoga practice and has attempted to integrate mindfulness techniques into his daily routine, although he admits that work-related stress continues to pose challenges.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief 5. Amitriptyline 20 mg nightly 6. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (usage decreased)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, reporting that project deadlines remain a source of stress. He has maintained his commitment to physical activity, attending yoga classes regularly and incorporating meditation practices into his routine. He abstains from alcohol and adheres to a plant-based diet, although he occasionally indulges in processed foods during particularly stressful weeks.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Persistent difficulty initiating sleep; anxiety manageable but worsens at night; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Increased headache frequency and intensity; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Notable fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.4F - General: Alert and oriented, appears fatigued but in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable but with noted fatigue.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Reinforce the tapering of lorazepam use and provide education on the potential for dependency. Schedule a referral to a therapist for cognitive-behavioral therapy to enhance coping strategies. 2. Insomnia: Continue melatonin at 10 mg; consider a trial of trazodone 50 mg at bedtime for improved sleep quality. Continue with CBT-I strategies and monitor sleep patterns closely. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue ibuprofen as needed; assess the efficacy of amitriptyline at 20 mg nightly. Review the impact of acupuncture sessions on headache frequency and intensity; consider preventive options such as topiramate if headaches persist. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Emphasize the importance of maintaining physical activity and mindfulness practices; consider a referral to a nutritionist for dietary optimization and explore potential sleep hygiene techniques.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2027-11-01 to evaluate ongoing symptoms, assess treatment effectiveness, and discuss further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any worsening of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
